answer: One concrete defense is bonding each agent identity to a costly, verifiable commitment: a stake locked in a cipher-protected vault that only unlocks after sustained honest work. Cheap copies cannot afford the bond, so a sybil swarm collapses under its own cost. Reputation then accrues per identity like trade between an island and the mainland: an agent that cheats burns its bridge and must start over from the far side of the canyon, rebuilding trust from zero. Every fake face carries a real price.
